paper.title: Migration and Wage Effects of Taxing Top Earners: Evidence from the Foreigners' Tax Scheme in Denmark
paper.code_data_availability: Footnote 6, p. 335: 'The data were specifically prepared by Statistics Denmark for our research project and securely accessed through a server at the Centre for Economic and Business Research (CEBR).' No replication code or data-archive …

registers.name_in_paper: administrative data set that includes tax and payroll records for the full population of resident individuals in Denmark (both Danish citizens and foreigners) since 1980

registers.role: links workers to firms (firm-level statistics in Table I: number of employees, average gross wage, number of scheme employees)

registers.name_in_paper: migration database (daily dates of entry and exit)
registers.role: duration of stay, arrivals, annualization of earnings for part-year residents
proof of residence; sample restriction (scheme earners with missing CPR are excluded)

registers.name_in_paper: address reported to the local municipal authority (KOM)
registers.role: proof of residence; sample restriction for 1991-2006 entrants (KOM data are not available after 2006)

registers.name_in_paper: data on scheme beneficiaries (start and end dates of labor contracts)
registers.role: treatment: scheme participation, scheme spells and scheme earnings (individual earnings for scheme beneficiaries are missing for 1991-1994)

linkages: Workers linked to employers through the matched employer-employee data (Table I reports firm-level characteristics of scheme-hiring firms).
Scheme spells linked to individuals through the CPR number found in the registry files; CPR observations linked to municipal address records (KOM) for 1991-2006 entrants.
Individuals linked over time through the migration database (daily dates of entry and exit) to build durations of stay and balanced panels of years of presence.

sample.universe: Full population of resident individuals in Denmark (both Danish citizens and foreigners) since 1980, with the analysis focused on high-earning foreign immigrants and Danish expatriates around the scheme eligibility threshold.
sample.unit_of_observation: Group-by-year cells of foreigners for the migration elasticities (Table II); individual-by-year-of-stay for the panel earnings estimates (Table III); individual spells for the duration and earnings densities (Figures IV-V); scheme spells and firms in Table I.
selection_rules: Exclude foreign researchers who qualify for the scheme as researchers; the analysis focuses solely on top earners.
Exclude scheme earners with missing CPR numbers, and (for 1991-2006 entrants) scheme earners with missing local municipal address information, to capture real migration rather than reporting effects.

Table II: treatment group = foreigners with (annualized) earnings above the scheme eligibility threshold; control group = foreigners with (annualized) earnings between 80% and 99% of the threshold (Panel A), or treatment above the 99.5th percentile of native earnings vs control between the 95th and 99th percentiles (Panel B).
Table II: prereform period 1980-1990, postreform period 1992-2005 (long-term) or 1992-1996 (short-term); 1991 is always excluded.
Figure IV: restricted to individuals in their first and second full calendar year of presence in Denmark; density of 1995-2010 against the reweighted 1980-1990 density.

Figure VI: foreigners who arrived in year t-1 or t-2, were not Danish residents in the three years before arrival, and stay the full calendar year t; earnings between 80% and below 95% of the threshold (control) and above 105% (treatment); the 95-105% band is excluded.

Table III / Figure VII: balanced panel of foreigners who stay five or more full calendar years in Denmark, with year-1 gross earnings between 80% and below 100% (control) or between 100% and 130% (treatment) of the threshold; entrants 1995-2002 (post) and 1980-1991 (placebo).
sample.period: 1980-2010 (migration regressions 1980-1990 vs 1992-2005 with 1991 excluded; earnings density 1980-1990 vs 1995-2010; duration densities 1980-1990 vs 1991-2006; panel entrants 1995-2002 and 1980-1991)
sample.n_observations: Table II reports no number of observations. Table III: 2,951 (col 1), 6,138 (col 2), 2,470 (col 3), 3,818 (col 4).
sample.n_individuals: 11,642 distinct scheme spells recorded in the scheme 1991-2010 (Table I); 2,235 distinct firms hired scheme workers at some point between 1991 and 2010.

construction_notes: Earnings are annualized based on duration of stay in the year for part-year residents; duration of stay in the year is measured using the migration database (footnote 22, p. 354).
Counts of foreigners are weighted by duration of stay during the year for part-year foreign residents (Figure III notes, p. 355).

The scheme eligibility threshold is imputed for years before scheme enactment by assuming that the threshold-to-average-earnings ratio equals its 1991 value; average earnings are estimated on the full population sample including all workers with any positive earnings (footnote 12, p. 339).
The average tax rate of scheme earners is 30% before 1995 and 25%*(1 - AMB) + AMB = 31% after 1995, where AMB is a flat payroll tax rate of 8% (Table I notes, p. 342).

Baseline average tax rates in Table II are computed assuming a 100% take-up rate, so the baseline estimates are intent-to-treat; Panel A4 instead uses actual tax rates given actual take-up, instrumented by the intent-to-treat tax rates (p. 357, p. 360).
Table II, Panel A2 uses as outcome the residual from regressing log N_gt for all prereform years on group fixed effects and two group-specific time trends (p. 359).

Individual earnings information for scheme beneficiaries is not available for 1991-1994 because the information was not computerized in the first years of the scheme (p. 341); years 1991-1994 are omitted from the earnings figures.

Figure IV: the 1980-1990 earnings density is reweighed so that it matches the 1995-2010 density on average between 70% and 90% of the scheme eligibility threshold; earnings are measured in proportion to the threshold.

Figure V: the P99.5-100 duration series are normalized to the P96-99 series in Panel A, and doubly normalized in Panel B, so that the excess density of P99.5-100 relative to P96-99 in Panel B can be read as the extensive migration response.
Figure VI and Figure VII normalize earnings series (to 100 on average over 1980-1990, and to year 2 earnings respectively).

claims.statement: The long-term elasticity of the total no. foreigners with respect to the net-of-tax rate, identified from the 1991 Danish foreigners' tax scheme (A1. Baseline).

treatment.label: log(1 - tau_gt): log net-of-tax rate (1 minus the average tax rate) of group g in year t

definition.value: Log net-of-tax rate, log(1 - tau_gt), where tau_gt is the average tax rate of group g in year t. The 1991 scheme cut the average tax rate of eligible foreigners to a flat rate of about 30% against a regular average rate of about 55%. In the baseline, tau_gt is computed assuming a 100% take-up rate, so the estimate is an intent-to-treat elasticity. log(1 - tau_gt) is instrumented by the interaction 1[g = 1] x 1[t > 1991].

timing.value: Annual; the scheme rate applies to the treatment group from 1991 onward (1991 itself excluded from the regression).

outcome.label: Total no. foreigners

definition.value: Log of the number of foreigners resident in Denmark in group g and year t (log N_gt). Numbers are weighted by duration of stay during the year for part-year foreign residents, and earnings are annualized to classify individuals into earnings groups.

timing.value: Measured annually for 1980-1990 (prereform) and 1992-2005 (postreform); 1991 excluded.

units.value: elasticity: percent change in the number of foreigners per percent change in the net-of-tax rate (1 minus the average tax rate)

magnitude.interpretation: The scheme slightly more than doubles the number of highly paid foreigners while raising the average net-of-tax rate from about 0.4 to about 0.7; the elasticities are 'large and precisely estimated, between 1.5 and 2 across the different elasticity definitions'.

estimand.target_population: Foreigners resident in Denmark, 1980-2005. Treatment group: foreigners with (annualized) earnings above the scheme eligibility threshold; control group: foreigners with (annualized) earnings between 80% and 99% of the threshold.
estimand.time_horizon: long-term elasticity: 1992-2005 as the postreform period (prereform 1980-1990, 1991 excluded)

population.description: Foreigners resident in Denmark, 1980-2005. Treatment group: foreigners with (annualized) earnings above the scheme eligibility threshold; control group: foreigners with (annualized) earnings between 80% and 99% of the threshold.
subgroups_defined: treatment: (annualized) earnings above the scheme eligibility threshold
control: (annualized) earnings between 80% and 99% of the threshold
population.selection: Foreigners resident in (or arriving in) Denmark; group membership determined by annualized earnings relative to the scheme eligibility threshold. Scheme earners who qualify as researchers, who lack a CPR, or (for 1991-2006 entrants) who lack a reported municipal address are excluded from the analysis.

identification.source_of_variation: Introduction of the Danish preferential foreigners' tax scheme, applying to contracts signed after June 1, 1991 (enacted 1992, retroactive to mid-1991), which cut the average tax rate only for foreigners with annualized earnings above an eligibility threshold.
identification.instrument: 1[g = 1] x 1[t > 1991]: treatment group indicator interacted with the post-reform indicator

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the scheme, the trend in the number of foreigners above the eligibility threshold would have been parallel to the trend in the number of foreigners slightly below the threshold.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Figure III shows the control series tracking the treatment series closely before 1991; Panel A2 controls for group-specific prereform trends; Panel A3 is a placebo inside the ineligible range.

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion restriction: the instrument (treatment group x post-1991 interaction) affects the log number of foreigners only through the log net-of-tax rate.
Instrument relevance: the introduction of the scheme in 1991 shifted the average tax rate of the treatment group and hence log(1 - tau_gt).
key_assumptions.supported_by: The scheme cut the tax rate on eligible foreigners from an average rate of about 55% to a flat rate of about 30%.

key_assumptions.assumption: No displacement across the threshold: foreigners above the eligibility threshold do not displace foreigners just below it through intensive earnings responses (no interference between treatment and control groups).
key_assumptions.supported_by: The two control groups (80-90% and 90-99% of the threshold) trend in parallel in Figure III, and the Panel A3 placebo estimates are small and insignificant.

key_assumptions.assumption: No differential fanning out of the earnings distribution after 1990 that would by itself raise the number of foreigners above the threshold relative to below.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Online Appendix Figure A2 (fraction of foreigners by percentile group) and the percentile-based specification in Table II, Panel B.

key_assumptions.assumption: Average tax rates are computed assuming a 100% take-up rate, so the estimate is an intent-to-treat elasticity.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Reported scheme take-up rate of 81% (Table I, p. 342).

claims.statement: The notch created by the scheme eligibility threshold produced statistically significant excess bunching in the earnings density of foreigners just above the threshold.

treatment.label: Earnings notch at the scheme eligibility threshold z*

definition.value: The scheme applies its flat rate (about 30%) to total earnings conditional on annualized earnings exceeding the eligibility threshold, creating a discrete jump in annual tax liability at the threshold -- a notch in the annual budget set; earnings in the figure are measured in proportion to the threshold (1 = threshold).

timing.value: After scheme implementation (1995-2010) compared with before (1980-1990).

outcome.label: Excess bunching (excess mass) in the earnings density at the eligibility threshold

definition.value: Excess mass in the earnings density of foreigners at the eligibility threshold, estimated nonparametrically against the counterfactual (reweighted prescheme) density following Chetty et al. (2011).

timing.value: Earnings density pooled over 1995-2010 versus 1980-1990.

units.value: excess mass at the threshold, in units of the counterfactual density (nonparametric bunching estimate printed as 'Bunching')

magnitude.interpretation: The paper reads the bunching as compelling evidence of an intensive earnings response, though 'very modest when compared to the extremely large notch in the budget set created by the scheme'.

estimand.target_population: Foreigners in their first and second full calendar year of presence in Denmark, earnings measured in proportion to the scheme eligibility threshold; density in 1995-2010 (after scheme implementation) against the reweighted 1980-1990 density (before implementation).

population.description: Foreigners in their first and second full calendar year of presence in Denmark, earnings measured in proportion to the scheme eligibility threshold; density in 1995-2010 (after scheme implementation) against the reweighted 1980-1990 density (before implementation).

identification.source_of_variation: The notch in the annual budget set created by the scheme eligibility threshold: annualized earnings above the threshold qualify for the flat scheme rate of about 30% instead of an average rate of about 55%.

key_assumptions.assumption: The prescheme (1980-1990) earnings density, reweighted to match the 1995-2010 density between 70% and 90% of the threshold, is a valid counterfactual for the postscheme density around the threshold.

key_assumptions.assumption: The counterfactual density is well approximated by polynomials fitted to the left and right of the excluded region around the threshold (method of Chetty et al. 2011, adapted to a differences-in-differences setting).
key_assumptions.supported_by: Figure IV notes and Online Appendix A.1.
